infra.login.title: Console sign-in
infra.login.subtitle: AWOG opens a browser so you can sign in with the same Account ID/alias + IAM username + password you use for the Console. No long-lived key, no terminal.
infra.login.reloginNameLocked: Refreshing the session for profile "{name}" — to rename it, edit the profile instead of signing in under a new name (that would create a second profile).
infra.login.nameTaken: A profile with this name already uses a different credential type — pick another name
infra.login.hint: Click sign in, then finish in your browser. The password only goes to AWS — AWOG never sees or stores it.
infra.login.staleCookieHint: If the sign-in page shows "400 Bad Request": this is caused by stale AWS cookies in your browser, not by anything you or AWOG did wrong. Once you press sign in, AWOG shows the authorize URL together with an "Open a private window" button — use it to sign in again in a clean window.
infra.login.waiting: Waiting for you to sign in in the browser…
infra.login.url.title: Sign-in URL (if the browser did not open, or the page errors)
infra.login.url.privateOpened: Opened {browser} in a private window — sign in there.
infra.login.url.privateNoBrowser: No browser on this machine can open a private window from the command line (Safari cannot). Copy the URL and paste it into a private window instead.
infra.login.url.privateFailed: Could not open a private window. Copy the URL and paste it into a private window instead.
infra.login.url.hint: Stale AWS cookies in your main browser are what cause the 400 Bad Request page. Click "Open a private window" to sign in in a clean window — it comes back to AWOG by itself when you are done.
infra.login.errTimeout: Timed out after 5 minutes before sign-in finished, so this attempt has stopped — usually the 400 Bad Request page. Press sign in again and use "Open a private window" in the URL box that appears, or read the tip below if you sign in often.
infra.login.retryNote: Opening a private window every time gets tedious: sign in to the Console in your main browser once (button below) so the session is fresh — `aws login` reuses it, and next time it is a single click. If the private window itself fails too, cookies are not the cause: the IAM user needs the SignInLocalDevelopmentAccess policy — ask your AWS administrator.
infra.login.done: Profile "{name}" is ready — no further setup needed.
